data.source: SafeBench simulation platform; 261 driving videos collected by the authors from YouTube (Sec. 3.1); code at github.com/TrafficComposer/TrafficAlign; exact prompts only in Supplementary Material

notes: Two live models are used as pipeline components: gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 synthesizes NL scenario descriptions from driving-video frames, and gpt-5-2025-08-07 translates them into a DSL. The paper's headline claims (10.8% more collisions, 36.1% reduction after fine-tuning) are downstream RL-driving-agent metrics from a SafeBench-style simulator, not direct LLM outputs, so re-execution needs a full simulator/RL harness in addition to the API calls. The cleanest single-model-attributable number is the Table 2 ablation using bare GPT-5 (no TrafficAlign alignment step) as one of five baseline scenario generators; a comparable GPT-4o row uses gpt-4o-2024-11-20, which is not on the live list.
